title: Wallet credit and PawPoints stack to 120% of the order value on one booking
actor: The CUSTOMER themself. Real platform session cookie issued by lib/platform-session.ts issuePlatformSession over a verified customer_otp identity binding (subjectType=customer, subjectId=CUST-STACK); not a preview actor, not staff. Only prerequisite is any non-zero wallet balance and any non-zero PawPoints balance, both of which staff hand out routinely (refund/cancellation/goodwill credit, service-recovery points).
request: Two REAL route handlers, same booking, same customer session. (1) POST /api/pawspace-wallet {"bookingId":"BK-STACK"} with cookie + same-origin header -> redeemWalletForBooking. (2) POST /api/paw-points {"bookingId":"BK-STACK","points":5000} with the same cookie -> redeemPoints. Setup used the real staff routes: POST /api/pawspace-wallet {action:'credit',customerId:'CUST-STACK',amount:5000,source:'goodwill',idempotencyKey:'wc-1'} as maker (ops-staff@pawspace.test, 202) then {action:'credit',requestId:'WCR-...'} as a distinct checker (fin-checker@pawspace.test, 201); POST /api/paw-points {action:'grant_goodwill',customerId:'CUST-STACK',points:5000,reason:'service recovery probe'} (201).
response: wallet redeem 201 {"data":{"bookingId":"BK-STACK","walletUsed":4545.45,"bonus":454.55,"appliedValue":5000,"balance":454.55}} ; points redeem 201 {"data":{"bookingId":"BK-STACK","pointsRedeemed":2000,"discountApplied":1000,"balance":3000}}. Neither call refused, neither knew about the other.
d1_before: canonical_bookings: {id:'BK-STACK',customer_id:'CUST-STACK',total_amount:5000,status:'confirmed'}. pawspace_wallet_accounts: balance 5000. paw_points_ledger: one 'goodwill' row +5000 points.
d1_after: pawspace_wallet_ledger: [{entry_type:'credit',amount:5000,applied_value:0,balance_after:5000},{entry_type:'redeem',amount:-4545.45,bonus_amount:454.55,applied_value:5000,balance_after:454.55}]. paw_points_ledger: [{entry_type:'goodwill',points:5000},{entry_type:'redeemed',points:-2000}]. canonical_bookings.total_amount is STILL 5000 and status still 'confirmed' - neither redemption writes the booking down. Finance journal (lib/finance-accounts postJournal) posts CREDITS_APPLIED credit 5000 for the wallet leg; the PawPoints leg posts no journal at all.
repeatable: Yes - executed twice, identical Rs.6000-on-a-Rs.5000-booking result both runs.
canonical_failure: redeemWalletForBooking and redeemPoints each compute their cap independently against canonical_bookings.total_amount and neither writes the booking down, so the two credit instruments applied to the same booking sum to Rs.6,000 of discount on a Rs.5,000 order - 120% of order value - and lib/unit-economics.ts then books all Rs.6,000 as real discount against a Rs.5,000 GMV line.
blast_radius: Every customer holding both instruments, self-service, no staff involvement, one HTTP call each. PawPoints' MAX_REDEEM_FRACTION=0.2 margin cap is measured on the gross total, so it survives intact even after the wallet has already covered 100% of the booking. With a governed coupon in the mix the coupon has already reduced canonical_bookings.total_amount, so wallet+points then re-apply against the NET figure and the combined giveaway exceeds the order value by even more. lib/unit-economics.ts sums coupon_redemptions.discount_amount + paw_points_ledger*0.5 + pawspace_wallet_ledger.applied_value into `discounts` against a GMV taken from total_amount, so contribution goes negative and no report flags the over-application. Rs.1,000 lost per Rs.5,000 booking in this exact probe; scales with wallet balance because the 10% WALLET_BONUS_RATE also inflates appliedValue above the credit actually held.
regression: tests/money-hardening.test.mjs :: "REGRESSION lib/pawspace-wallet-governance.ts + lib/paw-points-governance.ts: wallet and points together cannot exceed the order value" + "REGRESSION: the same ceiling holds when points are redeemed first" + "REGRESSION: each instrument alone still works, and the margin cap is unchanged"
fix_note: Each redemption now caps against what is still PAYABLE on the booking rather than against the gross total, via a new lib/booking-credit-application.ts that reads what every instrument has already applied (pawspace_wallet_ledger.applied_value plus paw_points_ledger converted at the shared REDEEM_RUPEE_PER_POINT). PawPoints' MAX_REDEEM_FRACTION margin cap is unchanged and still measured on the gross total; the tighter of the two now binds. Order does not decide the outcome - the defect was symmetric and both directions are covered. No incentive policy is invented: each instrument alone behaves exactly as before, including the wallet's 10% bonus and the 20% points cap.

title: Concurrent grooming completion consumes two subscription sessions for one delivered service
actor: Any actor that can complete a grooming job: requirePermission(actor,'bookings.view') + requireProviderOwnership for the work order's provider - i.e. the assigned PROVIDER in the provider app, or ops staff. Probe used a forwarded-identity staff actor (oai-authenticated-user-email: ops-staff@pawspace.test, role founder). No preview, no elevated money permission needed.
request: Two concurrent POST /api/grooming-lifecycle {"bookingId":"BK-SESS","action":"complete"} issued with Promise.allSettled against the REAL exported POST handler (env PAWSPACE_MEDIA_ENV='uat' so the synthetic proof refs uat://proof/BK-SESS/before|after validate). Booking status 'in_service', one grooming session reserved against a 10-session subscription GSUB-1.
response: BOTH calls returned HTTP 200. Both bodies report subscriptionUsage {sessions_reserved:1, sessions_consumed:1, status:'consumed'} - the response shows a single consumption while the subscription counter has moved twice. Two 'service_completed' booking_lifecycle_events rows were written.
d1_before: customer_grooming_subscriptions GSUB-1: {total_sessions:10, sessions_reserved:1, sessions_consumed:0, status:'active'}. booking_subscription_usage BK-SESS: {sessions_reserved:1, sessions_consumed:0, status:'reserved'}.
d1_after: customer_grooming_subscriptions GSUB-1: {total_sessions:10, sessions_reserved:0, sessions_consumed:2, status:'active'}. booking_subscription_usage BK-SESS: {sessions_reserved:1, sessions_consumed:1, status:'consumed'}. Available = 10-0-2 = 8 where it must be 9. The usage ledger and the subscription counter now disagree by one session.
repeatable: Yes - executed twice, sessions_consumed=2 and available=8 on both runs.
canonical_failure: In app/api/grooming-lifecycle/route.ts the guarded usage flip (UPDATE booking_subscription_usage ... WHERE status='reserved') and the UNGUARDED counter move (UPDATE customer_grooming_subscriptions SET sessions_reserved=MAX(0,sessions_reserved-?),sessions_consumed=sessions_consumed+? WHERE id=?) sit in the same db.batch, so a caller that loses the flip race still runs the counter update and consumes a second session that was never delivered.
blast_radius: This is the exact defect already fixed inside lib/subscription-wallet.ts - its consume branch carries the comment 'Previously both statements sat in one batch, so a lost race still ran the unconditional counter update and double-counted the consumption' and now runs the flip first and checks meta.changes. The identical pattern was left in app/api/grooming-lifecycle/route.ts, which is the path every real grooming completion actually takes. The route's other completion writes are all INSERT OR IGNORE / idempotent, so a double-tap, a provider-app retry or a duplicated request is otherwise harmless - this is the one write that is not. Consequence per race: the customer silently loses one prepaid grooming session (on a 10-session plan priced around Rs.12,000 that is roughly Rs.1,200 of entitlement destroyed), and the subscription reaches 'exhausted' one session early. The in-line comment in the route asserting 'Double-consumption stays impossible via the usage row's status=reserved guard above' is false for the second statement, which that guard does not cover.

title: Referrer's configured monthly reward ceiling is exceeded by two concurrent qualifications
actor: Two paths, neither privileged. (1) Staff: POST /api/referral-governance {action:'qualify'} requires only bookings.manage. (2) NO STAFF AT ALL: app/api/grooming-lifecycle's `complete` action calls referralQualification -> tryQualifyLinkedReferral -> qualifyReferralClaim automatically, so two PROVIDERS completing two different referred friends' first bookings at the same moment fire it. Probe drove the real lib function qualifyReferralClaim directly with actorId 'staff@probe'.
request: Programme 'uat-referral-programme' saved active through the real saveReferralProgramme with friendDiscount 500, referrerReward 500, perReferrerMonthlyLimit 1, rewardValidityDays 30, reversalOnRefund true. One referral code for REFERRER, three claims (FRIEND-1/2/3) through the real claimReferral. Two friends' first bookings BK-F2 and BK-F3 set completed with captured booking_payments. Then Promise.allSettled([qualifyReferralClaim(claim FRIEND-2, BK-F2, key 'q2'), qualifyReferralClaim(claim FRIEND-3, BK-F3, key 'q3')]).
response: BOTH fulfilled. qualify#0 -> {id:'RWD-...-E80',amount:500,status:'released',sourceBookingId:'BK-F2'}; qualify#1 -> {id:'RWD-...-719',amount:500,status:'released',sourceBookingId:'BK-F3'}. Neither returned the 'Configured monthly reward limit reached' held state the code is written to produce.
d1_after: referral_rewards: [{id:'RWD-...-E80',referrer_customer_id:'REFERRER',amount:500,status:'released'},{id:'RWD-...-719',referrer_customer_id:'REFERRER',amount:500,status:'released'}] - 2 released rewards this calendar month against a configured limit of 1. referral_claims: both 'qualified'. referral_reward_events: 4 rows (pending+released for each).
repeatable: Yes - executed twice, 2 rewards / Rs.1,000 both runs.
canonical_failure: qualifyReferralClaim reads the referrer's month-to-date reward count with a plain SELECT COUNT(*) and then inserts the new referral_rewards row in an UNGUARDED db.batch, so two qualifications that interleave at that await both see count 0 < limit 1 and both issue a reward.
blast_radius: Directly doubles (or N-times, with N concurrent qualifications) the referrer reward liability that perReferrerMonthlyLimit exists to cap. In this probe Rs.1,000 was released against a Rs.500 configured monthly ceiling. The per-claim guards that DO exist (referral_rewards.claim_id UNIQUE, source_booking_id UNIQUE) stop the same claim being rewarded twice but say nothing about the cross-claim monthly cap, which is the only thing standing between a referrer and unbounded reward farming: sign up N friends, have their first bookings completed in the same window, collect N rewards in a month capped at 1. The comparable coupon ceiling in lib/coupon-governance.ts is enforced correctly, by putting the count inside the INSERT's subquery so a NOT NULL abort rolls the batch back - referral rewards were not given the same treatment. It is worse than a staff-only race because app/api/grooming-lifecycle fires qualification automatically on service completion, so ordinary provider traffic triggers it.

title: A referral claim still discounts a booking after its programme is paused, out of window, and its discount set to zero
actor: The referred CUSTOMER, at booking time. app/api/canonical-bookings passes input.pricing.referralClaimId straight into prepareReferralBooking for the customer's own first booking; no staff and no extra permission is involved. Probe drove the real exported lib function prepareReferralBooking.
request: prepareReferralBooking(db,{claimId:'RCL-...-145',customer:{id:'FRIEND-1',primaryPhone:'9000000011',email:'friend-1@probe.test'},serviceCode:'grooming',cityId:'blr',baseAmount:2000,baseAmountDueNow:2000,hasOtherOffer:false,isSubscription:false}) - issued AFTER the owning programme was paused, its validity window moved wholly into the past, and its friend_discount set to 0.
response: ACCEPTED: {discountAmount:500, totalAmount:1500, baseAmount:2000, code:'REF-...'} - a Rs.500 discount from a programme that is paused, expired by 300 days, and configured to give Rs.0.
d1_before: referral_programmes 'uat-referral-programme': {status:'paused', valid_from: now-400d, valid_until: now-300d, friend_discount:0}. referral_claims RCL-...-145: {status:'pending_booking', fraud_state:'clear', policy_snapshot_json:{...friendDiscount:500...}} - the snapshot frozen when the claim was made while the programme was still active.
d1_after: No refusal, no write blocked. The caller (app/api/canonical-bookings) proceeds to write the booking at totalAmount 1500 and pushes referralBookingLinkStatement + referralClaimBoundStatement into the booking batch, so referral_claim_booking_links records applied_discount 500 and the claim moves to 'pending_completion'.
repeatable: Yes - executed twice, Rs.500 accepted both runs.
canonical_failure: prepareReferralBooking validates only the CLAIM row (status, fraud_state, customer, service/city, first-booking, identity collision) and reads friendDiscount out of the claim's frozen policy_snapshot_json - it never re-reads referral_programmes, so a paused programme, an elapsed validity window and a changed or zeroed friend discount are all invisible at redemption time.
blast_radius: Expiry and programme shutdown are enforced only at CLAIM time (claimReferral checks status, requireActiveConfiguration and the validity window) and in the listing surfaces - not at the moment money is given away. Every claim ever created stays redeemable forever at its original discount: pausing a programme, letting it expire, or cutting the friend discount does not stop outstanding claims, and marketing has no way to stop the bleed short of individually rejecting each claim through reviewReferralClaim. There is also no claim-level expiry column at all - referral_claims has no valid_until - so a claim made today is still worth its original rupees years later. This is the 'absent treated as satisfied' class: the absent programme re-check reads as an approved programme. The rupee consequence is the full snapshot friendDiscount per stale claim (Rs.500 here), unbounded in the number of stale claims.
